newsitem.title: USA: U.S. weekly rice cash market summary -- USDA.
newsitem.headline: U.S. weekly rice cash market summary -- USDA.

text.p: In the South, rice prices were steady to weak. Long grain milled rice prices were selling mostly at $19.50 per cwt, however some discounts of up to $1.00 were reported. Medium grain traded mostly at $18.00- $19.00, Second heads were steady at $14.00-$15.00 and Brewers remain in very tight supply with few quotes at $14.50-$15.50. Rice by-products were uneven, bran was steady to $10.00 higher, millfeed was mostly steady to $2.00 lower.
In California, rice prices were steady with Medium grain selling mostly at $19.50. Rice bran was $10.00-$20.00 lower.
California rice ship loadings: For the week ending December 14, 1996, at the Port of Sacramento the Fellow loaded 26,400 mt of U.S. No 1 bulk Medium grain milled rice for Turkey.

Inspections of California rice for export: There were 582,278 cwt of U.S. Medium Grain milled rice inspected for the week ending December 14, 1996. The yearly total since October 1, 1996 is 2,204,591 cwt compared to 1,294,460 cwt a year ago.

The following prices were for domestic shipment -- offers, FOB mills, milled rice, dollars per cwt, bagged. (All milled rice grade 2 not to exceed 4 percent brokens, except California grade 1. All second heads grade 4 or better)
